_comment: Empathize social-interaction text. Structure (ids, tone, baseDelta, tier, deltas, toneMult) lives in js/db/NPC/SocialLines.json; this file carries only the prose and is deep-merged over it per language by NPCEmpathize.js. {name} = NPC name.

praise.label: Praise
player: You handled that better than anyone I know, {name}.
Honestly, {name}, you're one of the sharpest people here.
I've seen a lot of folks, but you stand out, {name}.
That was genuinely impressive, {name}.
People should pay more attention to what you do, {name}.
You've got real talent, {name}. Don't waste it.
responseGood: ...Thank you. I needed to hear that.
That's kind of you to say.
Not many people notice. I appreciate it.
Coming from you, that means something.
responseBad: You say that every single time. It's losing its shine.
More flattery? I'm not a fool.
If you praise everything, you praise nothing.
Save it. I've heard this speech already.
What are you buttering me up for?

compliment.label: Compliment
player: That's a good look on you, {name}.
You've got great taste, {name}.
I like the way you carry yourself, {name}.
You always seem so put-together, {name}.
There's something reassuring about you, {name}.
You make this place a little brighter, {name}.
responseGood: You've made my day a bit better.
responseBad: You're laying it on thick again.
Every day the same compliment. It rings hollow now.
Flattery gets stale, you know.
Uh-huh.
What do you want from me?

encourage.label: Encourage
player: Don't give up, {name}. You've got this.
Whatever you're facing, {name}, you can handle it.
Keep going, {name}. It gets easier.
I believe in you, {name}. Truly.
You're stronger than you think, {name}.
One step at a time, {name}. You'll get there.
responseGood: I needed someone to say that.
That helps more than you know.
Okay. Okay, I can do this.
responseBad: Empty words, said too often.
You keep cheering, but you never actually help.
I've heard the pep talk already.
Encouragement without substance.
Please, not this again.

flatter.label: Flatter
player: Surely someone as clever as you already knows this, {name}.
A person of your standing deserves the best, {name}.
They'd be lost around here without you, {name}.
You're clearly the most capable one in the room, {name}.
I only trust someone as wise as you, {name}.
Everyone speaks so highly of you, {name}.
responseBad: Now you're just being oily.
I can smell flattery a mile off.
What's your angle?
Too much honey turns the stomach.
Do you think I'm that vain?

thank.label: Thank
player: Thank you for everything, {name}.
I owe you one, {name}. Really.
I won't forget your kindness, {name}.
You've been a real help, {name}. Thanks.
I'm grateful for you, {name}.
Cheers, {name}. I mean it.
responseGood: It was nothing, but... thank you.
responseBad: You thank me, but you never return the favor.
Words are cheap.
Gratitude again? Show me, don't tell me.
Hmph. Thanks and nothing else.
I'd rather you actually did something.

smalltalk.label: Small Talk
player: Busy day, {name}?
How are things around here, {name}?
Anything new with you, {name}?
Keeping well, {name}?
Long week, huh, {name}?
So, how's life treating you, {name}?
responseGood: Same as always, but I can't complain.
Oh, you know. One thing after another.
responseBad: We talk about nothing every time.
Small talk again? Is that all you've got?
I'm a little busy for chit-chat.
Fine, fine, always fine.
You could just say what you actually want.

gossip.label: Gossip
player: Heard anything interesting lately, {name}?
People have been talking, {name}. Have you heard?
Between us, {name}, what's the word on the street?
You always know the rumors, {name}. Spill.
Any juicy news around here, {name}?
Come on, {name}, tell me something I don't know.
responseGood: You didn't hear it from me.
Oh, I've got a few things.
responseBad: I don't trade in gossip with you anymore.
You're always digging.
That's how rumors about ME start.
Careful. Loose talk cuts both ways.
Not this time.

weather.label: Comment on Weather
player: Strange weather we're having, {name}.
Bit of a chill in the air today, {name}.
Think the rain will hold off, {name}?
Lovely sky today, isn't it, {name}?
Never can trust the forecast, eh, {name}?
Good day to be outside, {name}.
responseGood: Makes you want to stay in, doesn't it.
responseBad: The weather. Again. Riveting.
Is the sky all we ever discuss?
Yes. Weather exists.
Truly gripping conversation.
...And?

insult.label: Insult
player: You're a waste of space, {name}.
Honestly, {name}, you're pathetic.
I've met rocks smarter than you, {name}.
You're an embarrassment, {name}.
Nobody actually likes you, {name}.
You're useless, {name}, and everyone knows it.
responseGood: ...What did I ever do to you?
responseBad: Insults again? You're predictable.
Is that all you know how to do?
You're not worth my anger anymore.
Keep talking. One day I'll answer.
Every time. You're pitiful.

mock.label: Mock
player: Nice work, {name}. Did you practice failing?
Oh, brilliant plan, {name}. Truly inspired.
Wow, {name}, you must be so proud of yourself.
Careful, {name}, all that thinking might hurt you.
Cute effort, {name}. Adorable, really.
Bravo, {name}. A performance for the ages.
responseGood: Keep mocking. See where it gets you.
responseBad: Your jokes got old a while ago.
Same tired mockery.
Try harder.
I've stopped listening to you.
You're the joke now, honestly.

criticize.label: Criticize
player: You could have done that far better, {name}.
That was sloppy work, {name}.
I expected more from you, {name}.
You're cutting corners, {name}. It shows.
Frankly, {name}, that wasn't good enough.
You keep making the same mistakes, {name}.
responseBad: You criticize but never lift a finger yourself.
Always the expert, aren't you.
Nothing satisfies you.
I'm sick of your nagging.
Save your lectures.

threaten.label: Threaten
player: Cross me and you'll regret it, {name}.
You don't want me as an enemy, {name}.
Watch yourself, {name}. I'm warning you.
One wrong move, {name}, and it's over for you.
I could make your life very difficult, {name}.
Remember who you're talking to, {name}.
responseBad: You threaten, but you never follow through.
Empty threats.
You again? I've stopped being scared.
Do your worst.
Careful. My patience is gone.

flirt.label: Flirt
player: So, {name}, does anyone around here ever manage to keep up with you?
You lean in a little. "I was hoping you'd be here, {name}."
"Careful, {name}. I could get used to this."
"You've been on my mind more than is strictly reasonable, {name}."
responseGood: Keep talking like that and I might believe you.
responseBad: Let's pretend you didn't say that.
That line works on somebody, I'm sure. Not on me.
I'd rather keep this friendly.
No.

admire.label: Admire Them
player: "Whoever told you that suits you was right, {name}."
You catch yourself staring. "Sorry. You're just, hard to look away from."
"There's something about the way you carry yourself, {name}."
"You walked in and the room got smaller," you tell {name}.
responseGood: Well. Now I'll be thinking about that all day.
responseBad: I'd rather be noticed for something else.
You've been looking, then.
People say that when they want something.
Please don't.

loveLetter.label: Slip a Love Letter
player: You press a folded letter into {name}'s hand and step back before you can regret it.
"Don't read it here," you say, handing {name} a sealed note.
You leave a letter where {name} will find it, sealed with a clumsy wax stamp.
"I wrote this badly three times," you admit, giving {name} the fourth attempt.
responseGood: Nobody's written to me in years.
You wrote all this? For me?
Three drafts. It shows. I like that.
responseBad: I don't think I should read this.
This is a lot.
You barely know me.
I'll be keeping this. As a reminder to be clearer with you.

serenade.label: Serenade Them
player: You take a breath and sing to {name}, badly, and entirely on purpose.
You start a song under {name}'s window, and commit to the whole verse.
"This one's yours," you say, and sing it to {name} in front of everyone.
You hum an old tune, then put {name}'s name in the chorus.
responseGood: Stop, stop, everyone's looking, don't stop.
That was awful. Do the last part again.
{name} listens all the way through, and doesn't say anything for a while after.
Nobody's ever embarrassed themselves for me before.
responseBad: Please. Stop.
You've made this everyone's business now.
{name} walks off halfway through the second verse.
That. Was a performance. It wasn't for me, it was at me.

askDance.label: Ask for a Dance
player: You offer {name} your hand. "One dance. Nobody has to know why."
"Dance with me, {name}. I'll lead badly, but I'll lead."
You bow, entirely too formally, and wait for {name} to take your hand.
"There's music somewhere," you tell {name}. "Close enough. Dance with me."
responseGood: One. And you're counting the steps out loud, clearly.
{name} laughs and steps in. They're a better dancer than you by a wide margin.
responseBad: No. Thank you.
I don't dance.
You're standing very close.
Ask someone who'd enjoy it.

holdHands.label: Take Their Hand
player: You reach out and take {name}'s hand, slowly enough that they could pull away.
Your fingers find {name}'s, and you leave them there.
"Is this alright?" you ask, hand hovering over {name}'s.
You lace your fingers through {name}'s without saying anything at all.
responseGood: {name} doesn't pull away. Their grip tightens, just slightly.
{name} looks at your joined hands like they're solving a puzzle, then relaxes.
responseBad: Don't.
You should have asked.
That's not, no.
I'm going to pretend that was an accident.

askOut.label: Ask Them Out
player: "Come out with me, {name}. Somewhere loud, or somewhere quiet, your call."
"One evening," you say. "You and me, {name}, and nothing else on the schedule."
"Let me buy you dinner, {name}. Badly cooked, honestly offered."
"I'd like to see you when neither of us is working, {name}."
responseGood: Took you long enough to ask.
responseBad: I don't think that would end well for either of us.
No.
I've enjoyed this. I'd like it to stay exactly what it is.
You misread something. That's on both of us.

confess.label: Confess Your Feelings
player: "I'm in love with you, {name}. I've been carrying it around for a while."
"I need to say this once, out loud, and then you can do what you like with it. I love you, {name}."
You stop pretending. "It's you, {name}. It has been for some time."
"I'd rather ruin this than keep lying about it," you tell {name}. "I love you."
responseGood: I know. I was waiting for you to say it first.
You picked a terrible moment. And I don't care at all.
responseBad: Oh. Oh, no. I'm sorry.
I wish you hadn't. Now I have to be honest back.
I don't feel that. I never did.
That wasn't fair. Putting that on me, here.

kiss.label: Kiss Them
player: You close the distance and kiss {name}.
You tilt {name}'s chin up and kiss them before the nerve runs out.
"Tell me to stop," you say, already leaning in toward {name}.
You kiss {name} like the conversation was only ever leading here.
responseGood: {name} kisses you back, hands fisted in your collar.
{name} makes a small startled sound, then pulls you closer.
{name} rests their forehead against yours and doesn't move for a moment.
responseBad: What is wrong with you?
No. Absolutely not.
You don't get to decide that for me.
Never do that again.

lines: I'm spoken for, and I intend to stay that way.
I'm with someone. Only someone. That's the whole arrangement.
I don't do this behind anyone's back.
You know I'm taken. And you asked anyway.
You're lovely. You're also not what I'm drawn to.
I don't think you've understood who I look at.
It isn't you. It's simply not how I'm wired.
That was never going to land. No offence meant.
I don't fall in love. Not with anyone. It isn't a wound, it's just true.
Romance is a language I've never spoken.
You want something I don't have to give. Friendship I can manage.
There's nothing there to reach. There never is.
Not that. Not with anyone, before you ask.
I don't want that kind of touch. From you or from anybody.
Talk to me all you like. That part is closed.
You're welcome to my company. And nothing else.
You're all warm and wet and unpredictable. I prefer a clean logic board.
No offence. But I only fall for things that hum.
Flesh does nothing for me. Bring me a chassis.
I've dated an arithmetic unit. You'd be a downgrade.
...Sorry. What were you saying?
You don't photosynthesise. It would never work.
I need someone rooted. Literally rooted.
My last partner was a hedge. We're still friends.
Too tall. Far too tall.
I have a type. And it comes with a beard and a mining claim.
Come back three feet shorter.
You're very kind. And much too long in the leg.
There's only ever been one man for me, and he built the Liminal Engine.
You're not Bubba Wilson.
Sorry. My heart belongs to an engineer from Ohio.
I've written him four hundred letters. He'll answer one day.

bubbaHimself.reasonLabel: is spoken for, by a goddess
lines: Whoa now, chiano chiano. You're the best friend I got in ninety-two dimensions. That's where it stops, darlin'.
There's one woman in my heart and she throws mountains. Ain't fair on you and it sure ain't safe.
I'm drivin' to Beagle to sign papers, not to start nothin'. Amice simme e amice restammo.
Guagliò, put that away 'fore the coffee pot jumps off the stove again. She watches, y'know. She always watches.
Darlin', I love you like a sister with a worse temper. That's the whole of it.
Nah, guaglio. We got somethin' better than that.
You want somebody who'll stay. I'm a man with a road under him. Ain't the same thing.
Madonna, and then who fixes the camper after she wrecks it? Be practical, Em.
{name} pretends, very badly, that he did not hear it, and talks about the manifold for ten minutes.

emZealot.reasonLabel: will not be courted by the god-killer
lines: You fed a god to a spear. You do not get to be charming.
I would sooner court the hole in the sky.
Not you. Never you.
Whatever you are now. It is not something I want closer.
You want love out of me. There is a queue, and it starts with the dead.
Court me. God is dead and the witch is flirting.
I have a wife, a mother and a parish. And all three would burn the bed.
{name} does not answer. {name} walks to the door and holds it open.
Not in this life. And there is no other one left to promise you.

emAnnoyed.reasonLabel: wants the famous witch to move along
lines: No. I've got enough weather in my life.
You'll be gone by Thursday and something will be on fire. That's the pattern.
I don't want to be a paragraph in your story.
Ask somebody who wants their name in the papers. Please. Anybody else.
Absolutely not. I have a business and a roof and I would like to keep both.
Of all the people in this town. Of all of them.
I would be in the papers by Friday. My mother reads the papers.
{name} says no in three words and finds work for their hands.
Find somebody who wants an interesting life. I had one. It was awful.

player: "I want something real with you, {name}. {style}, if you'll have it."
"I've been thinking about this. {style}, with you. Is that something you'd want?"
"{name}, I'm asking outright. {style}, the two of us."
You take a breath. "{style}, {name}. I mean it."
accept: I was hoping you'd ask. {style} sounds exactly right.
reject: I don't think I'm ready for that.
That's not what I want. Not with you, not like this.

story.label: Tell a Story
player: You settle in and spin a long tale about {subject}.
You tell {name} a winding story about {subject}.
"Let me tell you the tale of {subject}," you begin.
You recount an old legend concerning {subject}.
You weave a story of adventure and {subject} for {name}.
good: {subject}... what a tale. Tell me another sometime.
I could listen to you talk about {subject} for hours.
A fine story. You have a gift for it.
And then what? No, no, finish it later. Wonderful.
bad: {subject}? I've no patience for such stories.
That tale of {subject} bored me senseless.
Not to my taste at all.
Is this going somewhere? I have things to do.

poem.label: Recite a Poem
player: You clear your throat and recite a verse about {subject}.
You offer {name} a short poem on {subject}.
"A little verse, on {subject}," you say, and begin.
You recite a heartfelt ode to {subject}.
You improvise a rhyme about {subject} for {name}.
good: That verse on {subject} will stay with me.
bad: That rhyme on {subject} made my ears ache.
I don't much care for verse.
Was that meant to be serious?

landGood: Terrible. But I laughed. Damn you.
landGroan: That was awful. I sort of love it.
...I can't believe that worked on me.
flop: You've told me that one already.
templates: Why did {def:noun} {verb}? Because it was completely {adj~noun}!
{^indef:profession} walks into {indef:place} and says, "I'll have whatever's {adj}."
How many {noun*} does it take to {verb}? None, they're too {adj~noun}.
My {noun} is so {adj~noun}, even {def:profession} won't touch it.
What's the difference between {indef:noun} and {indef:noun2}? About {adj} coins.
I told my {noun} a secret, and now the whole {place} knows. Very {adj~noun} of it.
They say {def:place} is haunted by {indef:adj~noun} {noun}. I say it just needs {indef:profession}.

zealot.label: blames Em for the death of the Father
greeting: The witch. Naturally.
Every sacred word I owned died on New Year's Eve. And here you are, still breathing.
They say your memories were sharpened into a spear. Mine was a prayer that used to work.
You were the sacrifice. Sacrifices are meant to stay on the altar.
Kindling for a god-killing.
My mother had the last rites that took. Do the arithmetic yourself.
There. Now say what you came to say.
There were four masses in this town on a Sunday. There is one, and the priest reads it like a shopping list.
{name} sets down what they were holding, as though your being here required both hands free.
My brother went out to Ritual Island to look at the hole. He came back wrong and he came back quiet.
Habit. It used to be more than habit.
They say you flinch at church bells. Good. Something in you still knows what it did.
positive: Praise from you is a stain. I will wash it out later.
Flatter me for a year. My saints will still be silent.
Save the charm for the Guild. They already bought you once.
{name} accepts nothing, and makes a small warding gesture under the table.
You are kind to me the way a fire is warm. I have not forgotten what fires do.
And after the compliment? Do I get Him back?
I would rather be insulted honestly. Than flattered by the reason.
{name} thanks you in the flat voice kept for tax collectors.
You bought that charm with a memory that was not yours to spend. Keep it.
{name} notes the kindness the way one notes a symptom.
neutral: {name} answers in the fewest words the language allows, one hand on a pendant.
The weather. You want to discuss the weather. With me.
{name} talks to a point six inches to your left for the whole exchange.
Ask your questions of somebody with something left to lose.
Small talk. From the woman off the front page. Ask the wall. It has more patience.
{name} answers correctly, completely, and without once unclenching.
There is a word for conversation with your sort. I will not use it in the street.
{name} keeps a doorway behind them for the whole exchange.
Salt on the step, salt on the sill. Talk as long as you like. I did mine this morning.
{name} answers every question with the year it happened in, and nothing else.
negative: Yes. Say something ugly. It suits what you are.
{name} raises their voice so the whole street learns which witch is standing here.
Threaten me. There is nothing up there left to hear me scream.
Good. Now neither of us has to pretend.
You cannot damn me. That office is vacant. You saw to it.
{name} takes the insult like a blessing turned inside out, and repeats it under their breath.
Louder. I want witnesses to what came out of that mouth.
{name} does not answer, and begins, very deliberately, to pray at you.
Hurt me, then. Add it to the ledger. It is already unreadable.
Some of us still keep lists. Somebody has to.

annoyed.label: wishes Em would be famous elsewhere
greeting: You're the one out of the papers. Wonderful.
Whatever it is. Could you go and be it somewhere down the road?
I have eleven crates to shift and you have a legend to be. We're both busy.
Last time somebody like you came through, the sky did something. Move along.
No spells indoors. That's the whole rule.
No. Whatever it is. No.
{name} moves the till a little further from you, without comment.
You are the weather woman. Not the forecast sort. The other sort.
Two quiet months. That was the whole ambition.
If this is about the ritual, I was asleep. Same as everybody.
{name} serves the man behind you first, then you, then the man behind you again.
I have read the article twice, because people keep bringing it in. Congratulations.
positive: Lovely. Now go and be lovely two streets over.
Mm. Are you buying anything, or?
You're very nice for someone who blew a hole in heaven.
Yes, very good. Was there anything else?
{name} accepts the compliment the way one accepts a leaflet.
You are pleasant. So was the last one. He took the roof off.
{name} thanks you and starts restacking things that were already stacked.
Save it for whoever is printing you next.
{name} smiles with the lower half of the face only.
That will read beautifully. Local person charmed. Front page.
neutral: Rain later. That's the conversation.
{name} answers, checks the door, answers again, checks the door.
I don't follow the news and I'd rather it didn't follow me.
Fine. Same as yesterday. Same as tomorrow, if you would move along.
{name} answers you while looking past your shoulder for the queue.
You want the ordinary conversation. With you it never stays ordinary.
{name} gives you the shortest true answer available.
Roads are roads. Take one.
{name} keeps a hand on the shutter for the whole of it.
I have nothing worth quoting. Do try elsewhere.
negative: There it is. Go on then, curse the shop. Everybody else has.
Out. Take the weather with you.
You'll be gone by Thursday. I keep telling myself that.
Right. And that is the famous temper. Marvellous. Have it outside.
Say that to the ones who print you. They will pay for it.
Insult me all you like. The shop stays shut to you either way.
{name} begins counting down from ten in a very steady voice.
There it is. Now go and be it somewhere else.
{name} writes something on the back of their hand: your name, and a time.
You will be a story in this town for thirty years. And I will have to hear all of them.

fan.label: an invasive admirer
greeting: It IS you. Say the word. Say the one from the tabloid.
My cousin was on Ritual Island the week after. So we're practically family.
Sign it across the hole in the story.
Do the thing with the hands. The magic thing. Once. Please.
{name} has already turned to shout your name at somebody across the room.
I KNEW it was today. I had a feeling. I get feelings about you.
{name} shows you a scrapbook of your face cut out of four different papers, all of them the same photograph.
Is it true you cannot lift the spear? That is the part that gets me. That is the tragic part.
{name} calls you by a nickname the tabloids invented, thrilled to be first in the room with it.
My sister said I would never meet you and she is going to be SICK.
{name} touches your sleeve, then the coat, then apologises, then does it again.
Say something about the ninety-two percent. It does not have to be sad.
positive: She said that TO ME. You all heard it.
I'm going to repeat that word for word for the rest of my life.
{name} beams and asks whether they can walk with you. Just to the corner. Just to the next corner.
She was NICE to me. Nice.
{name} writes the compliment on the back of a receipt and puts it somewhere safe.
That is going on the wall, next to the photograph.
{name} asks whether they may tell people you said it, and does not wait for an answer.
Do you say that to everyone? No. Do not tell me. Let me have it.
{name} goes very red and shakes your hand three separate times.
Best thing to happen to me since the ritual.
neutral: Small talk. From Em. About BREAD.
{name} answers three questions you did not ask, all of them about you.
They said you'd be taller.
{name} nods along to a story about nothing at all, rapt, as though it were scripture.
What is the weather like where you are from? Not here. There. The other one.
{name} agrees with you enthusiastically before you have finished the sentence.
I am going that way too.
{name} asks four follow-up questions, none of them about the thing you said.
Tell me something ordinary about yourself.
{name} laughs at a part that was not funny, then checks whether the room caught it.
negative: She insulted me. That's better than the autograph.
Say it again, slower. I want to get it right when I tell it.
{name} laughs it off entirely. Nothing you do here is going to land.
You are allowed. After what you have been through, you are allowed anything.
{name} apologises to YOU for having been insulted.
That is the fire. That is what did for the Father, that right there.
{name} takes a small step back and then a large step forward.
Do it again, but with my name in it.
{name} treats the whole thing as a performance, and applauds at the end of it.
I have been shouted at by worse people for less.

clout.label: friendly because Em is famous
greeting: Em! Sit down, sit down. What are you drinking? On me.
I tell people I know you. Now it's technically true.
Stand there. No reason.
Between us. What really happened that night?
Em. EM. Everyone, this is Em.
{name} shakes your hand for a second longer than the handshake requires.
I always said the papers had you wrong.
{name} produces a chair from somewhere, and a story about a cousin who was nearly there.
You will want the good table.
{name} asks after your health at volume, and after your business quietly.
There is a man in the Guild you should meet. He would rather meet you.
I do not believe in any of it. But I believe in you, obviously.
positive: Coming from Em, that's practically a plaque.
{name} thanks you warmly and checks who was standing near enough to hear.
From Em, that. You all heard the lady.
{name} thanks you and immediately offers you something they cannot afford to give.
We are friends now, are we not. Say we are friends.
{name} writes it down. Not fondly. Accurately.
You must let me introduce you properly. To the right sort.
{name} laughs a beat too long, in the direction of the door.
That is the version I will be telling. And I will tell it better than it happened.
{name} pats your arm and glances at whoever has just come in.
neutral: {name} keeps the conversation going long past its natural end, glancing round to see who is watching.
We should do this properly some time.
{name} keeps you talking about nothing until somebody worth impressing walks past.
Fascinating.
{name} steers the conversation, gently and repeatedly, back to the night on Ritual Island.
I have been meaning to ask you something.
{name} agrees with your opinion, and then with the opposite one, from the next table.
Weather is in the papers today. So are you.
{name} offers to introduce you to people you can already see.
You must let me get the next one.
negative: {name}'s smile stays exactly where it is. Behind it, the friendship is being repriced.
Ah. She's got a temper. Marvellous.
Fair enough, fair enough.
{name} takes the insult publicly and cheerfully, which costs you more than it costs them.
She is allowed a temper. She has earned a temper.
{name} makes a joke of it and lets the room decide who won.
I will not fall out with Em over a word.
{name} looks briefly, genuinely stung, and then puts the face back on.

{name} raises a glass to you, and quietly stops recommending you.

gawker.label: treats Em as an exhibit
greeting: Ninety-two percent. Is it like a room with the furniture taken out?

May I ask you a difficult question.

They told me you flinch at bells. I moved the clock. Just in case.
{name} sits down opposite you with the air of somebody beginning a chapter.
You kept the birthdays and not the faces. I have thought about that all week.
positive: Interesting. Politeness survived the ritual. Not everything did.
{name} thanks you and asks, immediately, what praise feels like with most of a life missing.
Gratitude. Older than most of what they took, I should think.
{name} thanks you, and asks whether the compliment came from before or after.
You perform kindness very well.
{name} makes a small satisfied noise, as though a hypothesis had held.
That was warm. I did wonder whether warm had survived.

Go on, keep talking. I want to hear where the gaps are.

What was the weather like the day before?

Note the vocabulary. Intact. Fascinating.
Threat display. Intact. Proportionate, even.

You swear like somebody who learned it recently.
{name} does not move at all, which is worse than flinching.
Say it again when you are calm. And we will see whether it is the same sentence.
{name} writes one word, underlines it, and turns the page over.

genuine.label: sees the person, not the story

{name} greets you by name, correctly, and makes no performance of it.

That is good of you. I will take it at face value, if you do not mind.
{name} smiles properly, the way people smile when nothing is being counted.
You are better at that than the papers leave you room for.
{name} thanks you and changes the subject to something easy, deliberately.
Careful. I could get used to being spoken to like that.
{name} takes it, keeps it, and repeats it to nobody.
You could stop apologising for existing, you know. Only a thought.
{name} looks pleased, and a little sad on your behalf, and lets both of it show.
neutral: {name} talks with you about nothing at all, generously, for as long as you like.
No, go on. It's nice to hear you talk about something small.

negative: You've had a hard year. I'll take that as the year talking.
I'll forget you said that. If you'd like me to.
Do you want to try that again, or leave it?
That one landed. I will live. Sit down.
{name} does not answer in kind, which is somehow worse and somehow better.
You are allowed to be furious. Not at me, though, eh.
{name} puts the kettle on and says nothing whatsoever about it.
Right. That is the year talking again. I will wait.
{name} tells you plainly that it hurt, and then asks whether you are eating.
I would rather you shouted in here than out there. Out there they print it.

bubba.label: the only friend she has
greeting: Uè, Em! Set yourself down, guagliò, the Beast ain't goin' nowhere till that manifold cools.
Mannaggia, darlin', you look like eighty kilometres of bad road. Coffee's on the stove, 'a tazzulella is yours.
Jamme, get in. We're burnin' daylight and I'm burnin' oil.
Statt' bbuono, witch. Ain't nothin' in ninety-two dimensions comin' through that door while I got the wrench.
Beagle by Thursday, chiano chiano. Papers to sign, and then we see what the road wants.
If the coffee pot jumps off the stove again, that ain't you and it ain't me. 'A gelusia is a hell of a thing, darlin'.
She held. Told you she'd hold, guagliò.
Ue, look who the road spat out. Sit, sit. There is coffee and there is a chair, and one of them is clean.
This here has been tryin' to kill us since Tuesday. Not no more, guaglio.
You eat today? Don't lie to me, darlin', I can tell.
{name} has the radio on something with too much accordion in it, and no intention of changing it.
I dreamed about the Engine. She was singin'. That ain't good nor bad, darlin', that's just a sign.
Ninety-two percent gone and you still remember where I keep the ten mil. That's friendship, that is.
Siediti. You got that face like the sky said somethin' to you again.

Yeah, well. You ain't so bad yourself, guagliona.

Write that down, 'cause nobody's ever gonna believe I got told that.
Mannaggia, careful, darlin'. She hears nice words about me, she gets ideas, and then it rains rocks.
Hear that, Bestia? She likes us.
You want somethin', don't you. Nah. You don't. That's worse.
neutral: Weather's weather. Under eighty, whatever it does, it does.
{name} talks you through the Liminal Engine again, the whole of it, with the same joy as the first time.
Route 666 was worse. Ask me some time when we ain't drivin'.
Uagliò, pass me that spanner and keep talkin'. I listen better with somethin' in my hands.
Coffee first, problems after. That's the whole philosophy, guaglio.
{name} explains, at length, the difference between a noise that costs nothing and a noise that costs everything.
Bureaucracy in Beagle, madonna. Four stamps and a fella called Deniz who don't like me.
{name} argues with the radio for a while, and then agrees with it.

You can yell at me all you want, darlin'. I ain't goin' nowhere. Chiano chiano.
Ninety-two dimensions and you're still the second scariest woman I know.
Alright, alright, chiano chiano. Who are we mad at, and is it me?
You got a mouth on you today. Sit down, drink somethin'.
I been cussed at in two languages by a woman who throws mountains. You gotta try harder, darlin'.
{name} works straight through all of it, and hands you a cup at the end of it.
That one had teeth. Fine. We're still goin' to Beagle.
You wanna fight, fight the manifold. It started it.
refuseJoin: Me, ridin' along? Guagliò, somebody's gotta hold this camper together. I'll be right here when the road bends back.
I don't ride shotgun in my own life, darlin'. 'A Bestia don't drive herself.
She'd drop a mountain on whatever town we slept in. You go on ahead, Em. Chiano chiano.
Papers first, Beagle first. Then we talk about travellin' together like decent people.
Somebody's gotta keep the Engine honest, guaglio. That somebody has got my face.
I ain't much use out there. In here, with a wrench, I'm a whole army, darlin'.
Last fella who rode with me full-time got weather on him. Real weather. No thank you.
Ask me again after the papers are signed. Chiano chiano. Everything after the papers.

bubba.label: knows who built the Liminal Engine
greeting: You're him. You're the Liminal Engine man.
Wilson. My whole family rides a bus that works because of you.
An honour. A genuine honour.
They gave you the Nobel and you turned up here. Here. In this town.
That's the engine fella. That's him.
I read the lecture. Didn't understand a word past the first page, loved every one of them.

You compressed the road. People say it like it's simple. It is not simple.
Is she here? The Beast? Is she parked out front?

The man who put eighty kilometres an hour back in our pockets.

Mister Wilson. What can this place possibly do for you?

Don't you dare be humble about it. Not you.
He's kind as well. Of course he's kind as well.
I'm telling everyone about this. Everyone. My mother first.
Well now. Well, now.

Whatever you need in this town, you ask me. I mean that.

{name} nods along as though notes were being taken somewhere.

{name} hangs on the end of the sentence and looks faintly disappointed when it stops.

Wilson himself, talking to me about the weather.
You always this easy to talk to? Bet you are.
Anything you say is more interesting than what I was doing.
I'll take a plain word from you over a speech from anyone else.
negative: Ha! Right. Ha.
He's got a mouth on him. Look at that.
You're probably right. You usually are.
If Bubba Wilson says it, there's something in it.
Been called worse by men who never built anything.
Fair. Fair. I'll do better.
Bad day. Even geniuses get bad days, eh?
I'd take that from you and nobody else.
You've earned a temper. God knows what you carry around.

"I just kept turnin' it till it stopped arguin', guagliò. That's the whole trick."
"The Engine ain't mine no more. Belongs to whoever's drivin'."
"Mannaggia, don't start. I'm a mechanic that got lucky twice."
"Prize sits in a box under the bunk. Good bit of weight for holdin' a door."
"Weren't smarts, it were stubborn. There's a difference and it ain't in my favour."
"Anybody tell you I'm clever, ask 'em how many times she blew up first. Answer's eleven."
"Ue, you're kind. I'd rather hear about you, though, honest."
"I put an engine in a camper, that's all. The rest of it the road did."
"Statt' bbuono. Save the big words for somebody who deserves 'em."
"My hands did it, and my hands ain't takin' compliments today."
"Chiano chiano, now. You'll have me blushin' in front of the whole street."

I kept every clipping. There's a whole drawer. Is that mad? That's mad.

Twenty years. Twenty years of a drawer.
